title: When the market does not clear

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Define market disequilibrium, distinguish a surplus from a shortage, and trace how unsold stock or unmet buyers moves a market back towards equilibrium.

blocks.heading: Disequilibrium, surplus and shortage
blocks.text: Market disequilibrium is a position of a market in which the quantity demanded does not equal the quantity supplied at the prevailing price: the price sits above or below its equilibrium level. Above it, sellers offer more than buyers take - a surplus. Below it, buyers want more than sellers offer - a shortage. In Swakopmund, jam clears at N$30 a jar; held at N$40, jars demanded fall to 120 while jars offered rise to 180 - a surplus of 60 jars, since 180 - 120 = 60 jars.

blocks.heading: Measuring the gap at a price
blocks.text: The gap belongs to its price. The Swakopmund jam schedule: at N$20 a jar, 190 jars are demanded and 90 offered - a shortage of 100 jars, since 190 - 90 = 100 jars; at N$30, 150 and 150, no gap; at N$40, the surplus again. The woven-basket stall nearby shows the same working: with the equilibrium at N$45, a trader holding N$60 faces 60 baskets demanded and 90 offered, a surplus of 30 baskets, since 90 - 60 = 30 baskets. A noodle bar in Ho Chi Minh City pricing its bowls low shows the reverse: a queue, a shortage at work.

blocks.heading: How the pressure closes the gap
blocks.text: Take the shortage at N$20. Because buyers miss out, some of them are likely to offer more, and the price is bid up; as it rises, the quantity demanded eases along the demand curve while the quantity supplied stretches along the supply curve, and the gap narrows until the market is back at N$30 and 150 jars. A surplus works in reverse: unsold jars earn nothing, so the trader is likely to cut the price until the shelf empties. The pressure runs one way - a surplus presses the price down, a shortage presses it up - and the market tends back towards equilibrium.

blocks.heading: The test that tells them apart
blocks.text: The test is two readings: where the price sits against the equilibrium level, and which quantity exceeds which. Price above equilibrium, quantity supplied the larger - a surplus. Price below equilibrium, quantity demanded the larger - a shortage. The figures at the stated price settle it.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The curves that cross to set the equilibrium were drawn in topics 2.3 and 2.4; the gaps here are the market between equilibria.
